claims.text: A Si-20Cr-20Fe silicide coating can be deposited on MoNbTaTiW refractory high-entropy alloy by a fused slurry method.
The initial coating forms a bilayer with an MSi2-rich outer layer and an M5Si3-rich inner layer.
The deposited silicide coating is thin.
MoNbTaTiW is a tungsten-containing refractory high-entropy alloy suitable as the substrate.
The unmodified MoNbTaTiW microstructure is optimized for high strength and ductility.
The silicide coating effectively protects MoNbTaTiW from high-temperature oxidation.
During high-temperature oxidation, silicon diffuses from the coating into the MoNbTaTiW substrate and the inner silicide layer grows inward without a major structural change.
The coating layers are well adhered and coherent with the substrate.
The coating produces controlled interfacial nanostructures.
The silicide layers and their interface provide a thermal-conduction pathway.
The silicide coating provides better electron and phonon transport than the bulk high-entropy alloy substrate.
A well-bonded, coherent coating-substrate interface minimizes interfacial thermal resistance.
Lower interfacial thermal resistance enables more efficient heat dissipation.
Oxidation protection from the coating maintains the mechanical integrity of the underlying alloy.
The coated alloy will have higher effective thermal conductivity and better heat-transfer performance than an uncoated intermediate layer.
The coating will preserve the alloy's ultrahigh strength and ductility under plasma-facing operating conditions.
The proposed benefit should hold at temperatures from at least 1000 K to about 1600 K under long-duration cycling, transient heat fluxes, and irradiation by ionized species.
Performance may degrade at extreme temperatures or when delamination or uncontrolled oxidation occurs.
Coating thickness uniformity, interface quality, and long-term plasma stability will affect the magnitude of any thermal-conductivity improvement.
